- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is mildly negative or neutral (e.g., sentiment > -0.30), especially if recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate sharp price spikes in later forecast windows if sentiment turns positive (e.g., sentiment > 0.00) and recent prices are trending up — model tends to lag or underreact.
- Overshoot after strong positive sentiment spikes — model often peaks too early and then overcorrects downward, leading to overprediction in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after strong upward moves, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently overestimated in the first 5–7 days if sentiment is negative, then gradually correct — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate true price decline — should adjust downward by 1–2% per negative sentiment unit.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates the magnitude of the move — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.00.
